comments.note: EC-2 reveals a footgun: when strict:true is used WITHOUT check:true, all output files are written to disk before the throw. This means a strict-mode failure leaves partial build artefacts on disk that callers must clean up. The current behaviour is deterministic (all suites processed, then throw at the end) but the docs do not warn about this. Recommend adding a note to the build() JSDoc or README: 'Combine strict:true with check:true in CI to avoid leaving artefacts on disk when validation fails.' Alternatively, strict mode could short-circuit before writes — but that is a design decision for the code reviewer.

The default CC frontmatter template references {{cc_permission_mode}}, {{cc_model}}, and {{cc_memory}} — none of which are auto-derived by buildContext(). When the fixture _shared.yaml provides cc_permission_mode and cc_memory but not cc_model, [WARN] entries are emitted on stderr. This is expected and documented. Consider adding a 'Missing CC model — set cc_model in _shared.yaml or via a plugin' note to the default CC template's JSDoc to help new users.

EC-5 reveals that passing targets:[] is silently accepted and produces an empty BuildSummary rather than a validation error or warning. This is arguably correct (the build succeeded — nothing was asked), but a caller passing an empty array by mistake would get no feedback. A low-cost guard: if (targets.length === 0 && Object.keys(config.suites).length > 0) emit a [WARN] log.

comments.note: Fixed buildPersona() JSDoc pipeline step list in persona-builder.ts: steps 7-9 in the inline code comments (Assemble output, onPostRender, onValidate, Determine output path) were not reflected in the JSDoc, making it appear steps 7-8 jumped directly to plugin hooks. Updated the JSDoc to list all 12 steps explicitly so future maintainers understand the full pipeline without cross-referencing the inline comments.

Added strict+check footgun warning to build() JSDoc in persona-builder.ts. Both Developer and QA flagged this: when strict:true is used WITHOUT check:true, all output files are written before the throw (all suites are processed first, then the error is raised). This is deterministic and correct behaviour, but the undocumented side-effect leaves partial artefacts on disk for callers to clean up. Added clear JSDoc guidance: 'For CI usage, combine strict:true with check:true to avoid leaving partial artefacts on disk when validation fails.'

loadRawYaml() and the sharedPartialsDir/suitePartialsDir guards in buildSuite() use existsSync() (sync, from node:fs) as a pre-check before async readFile/loadPartials calls. This mixes the synchronous and async I/O models. The pattern is safe and race-condition-free in practice (single-process, single-threaded build), but a fully async approach using fs/promises.access() + try/catch would be more idiomatic. Consider consolidating in a future refactor.

buildContext() derives cc_file_name_stem via .replace(/\.md$/, ''). This correctly strips the trailing .md from values like 'my-persona.md' or 'my-persona.agent.md' (the latter gives 'my-persona.agent', which is the intended CC stem). If cc_file_name has no extension at all, the stem equals the full value — harmless fallback. No change needed, but worth documenting the intent: the strip is deliberately narrow (only .md, not .agent.md) to preserve the full dotted stem for CC naming conventions.

TargetType is exported from both src/plugins/index.ts and src/builders/index.ts (re-exported via types.ts). This dual public export is harmless — TypeScript deduplicates it — but creates mild confusion about the canonical import path. The builders/index.ts re-export is justified by the BuildConfig type docstring which promises that 'everything builder-related can be imported from a single module'. This is the right tradeoff; flagging for Documentation agent to note the canonical import path in any API reference.

[documentation-forward] build() JSDoc now documents the strict+check footgun inline. README or API reference should also carry a 'CI usage' note under the strict mode section, explaining that strict:true + check:true is the recommended CI pattern to ensure no artefacts are left on disk when validation fails.
